svg.desc: HydraBuzz Strategy A auto route, top-down on the BIOBUZZ field, red alliance: start on the garden wall in front of the hive, back up and launch, work the flower on the left wall, drive past the hive to the far side, launch twice with the far flower in between, and end near the loading zone.
svg.text: HydraBuzz, Strategy A auto: garden-side start, three launches, two flowers
Top-down, red alliance. On blue the same route is turned half a turn around the center of the field.
Front (the intake) on the garden wall, about 58 in
from the left wall, in front of the red hive. Four
pollen loaded. The launchers spin up at START.
Back up 11 in and hold. The gates open for 2 s
once the pollen wheel is past 2950 RPM.
Turn right to face the flower on the alliance wall
and drive to it. Back 9 in, arm out, stroke 8 in forward,
hold 1 s, back out, arm in. Intake roller on only here.
Drive 75 in up the left side, past the hive, turning
to face the far wall. Slide 26 in across to sit on the
far side of the hive, launchers toward it. Launch.
Drive to the flower on the far wall. Same routine.
Step back to the launch spot, 5 in from the last
Drive toward the loading zone and stop, facing
the far wall. VERIFY: as drawn it stops 3 in short of
the zone, so PARK is not certain.
route: Pedro paths, driven at full speed
launch: pollen out of the back of the robot
robot, 18 by 18 in: green edge intake (front),
flower on the wall, 4 pollen each; 1 tile = 24 in
Spots are the pose recorder’s numbers in AutoStrategyD.java, the route the team calls Strategy A (uncommitted, November 4): three LAUNCH steps
and two FLOWER steps. Field from Competition Manual Figure 10-2 (TU05): 6 by 6 tiles, hives in the center, a flower on each wall, gardens and
loading zones in the corners; zone sizes are approximate. The start spot is not in the code: 58 in from the left wall is read from where the
recorded route meets the two flowers. Measure it, and the end spot, on the field before the one-pager goes to a partner.
